subgroup_flags.classification_notes: All patients had ARDS by Berlin definition. Mean BMI 23 (ARDS) and 25 (ARDS+IAH), below 30, so non_obese_population. Timing: enrolled less than 72 hours after ARDS onset, but the exact interval from onset to balloon-guided titration is not reported and may exceed 48 hours, hence unclear. Ptp target is absolute end-expiratory transpulmonary pressure 0–10 cmH2O (Talmor method).

reported_subgroups.outcome_name: PaO2/FiO2 response to Ptp-guided vs ARDSnet PEEP
reported_subgroups.result_verbatim: In ARDS patients with IAH, the PaO2/FiO2, A–aDO2 and SaO2 with PEEP guided by Ptp improved significantly than ARDSnet protocol. In ARDS patients without IAH, there were no significant differences of PEEP induced change of gas exchange between PEEP guided by Ptp and ARDSnet protocol

provenance.quote: In ARDS patients with IAH, the PaO2/FiO2, A–aDO2 and SaO2 with PEEP guided by Ptp improved significantly than ARDSnet protocol. In ARDS patients without IAH, there were no significant differences of PEEP induced change of gas exchange between PEEP guided by Ptp and ARDSnet protocol (Table 3).
provenance.location: Results, Effects of PEEP on gas exchange of ARDS patients with and without IAH, p. 3237

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: Checked against all clusters in studies/COHORTS.md: no trial registration stated in this report; single centre (Zhongda Hospital, Nanjing, China); enrolment August 2011 to April 2012; no shared authors or institution with the epvent1/epvent2, mannheim_boesing, mgh_lung_rescue, or angers clusters. Concluded no overlap with any report in this review.
unclear_items: outcomes: 28-day mortality is reported only in Table 1 by IAH stratum (ARDS 25%, ARDS+IAH 33%, P=0.608), not by ventilation condition; because this is a crossover, mortality cannot be assigned to pes_guided or ardsnet_peep arm labels, so it is recorded here rather than as an outcome entry. Quote: '28-day mortality — 25% (ARDS n=8), 33% (ARDS+IAH n=7), P=0.608' (Table 1).

population.additional_baseline: Table 1 reports baseline characteristics per IAH stratum, which does not map to the crossover condition arm labels; stratum values were placed in name_verbatim with arm_label null.

intervention.balloon_calibration: the paper cites Baydur 1982 and describes the occlusion principle but does not explicitly state an occlusion test was performed on these patients, nor the balloon filling volume; coded baydur_occlusion_test on the described mechanism.
design.randomised: stated as randomized crossover, but the randomised element (order of the two PEEP methods) is shown only in Figure 2; sequence_position left null for both arms.
feasibility.n_placement_successful: balloon insertion described for all 15 patients and measurements appear complete, but successful placement is not explicitly stated, so left null.
adults_18_plus: age exclusion criteria stated explicitly, so coded yes; no ambiguity.
Results text reports 'PEEP induced recruitment volume increased 207 ml by Ptp' (p. 3237) in ARDS+IAH patients; no per-arm table values, recorded here only.
Figure 3 reports Crs, Ccw, Cl and VD/VT under baseline, ARDSnet and Ptp conditions only graphically; no numeric values extractable from the text layer.
data_only_in_figure: Figure 3A: Crs (ml/cmH2O) at baseline, ARDSnet protocol and Ptp, ARDS vs ARDS+IAH
Figure 3B: Ccw (ml/cmH2O) at baseline, ARDSnet protocol and Ptp, ARDS vs ARDS+IAH
Figure 3C: Cl (ml/cmH2O) at baseline, ARDSnet protocol and Ptp, ARDS vs ARDS+IAH
Figure 3D: VD/VT at baseline, ARDSnet protocol and Ptp, ARDS vs ARDS+IAH
extraction_flags.general_notes: Randomised crossover physiologic study in 15 ARDS patients stratified by intra-abdominal hypertension; every patient received both Ptp-guided and ARDSnet-guided PEEP for 30 minutes each. 28-day mortality (25% ARDS, 33% ARDS+IAH, P=0.608, Table 1) is reported by stratum only and cannot be attributed to a ventilation condition in this crossover design. Lung recruitment volume increased 207 ml with Ptp vs ARDSnet in ARDS+IAH patients (Results text, p. 3237). No adverse-event or balloon-complication reporting anywhere in the paper.
